intent: Deliver the iteration 7 and 9 design, the best known result (score 75.92, reproduced exactly), as the final candidate. Change nothing from iteration 9. Integrator: keep kp 3.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.2, base_speed 2.0, last_direction line-loss recovery, and the 25-times-x sensor weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2). Expected result on the development tracks: oval progress about 0.27, s-bend progress about 0.157 with oscillation about 0.135, slalom progress about 0.109 with 1.0 line loss per run. The unseen track is unknown, so the expected score there is uncertain.
learning: Across iterations 7 to 10, the best oval result was not monotonic in mass (0.5 gave 0.12, 0.6 gave 0.2725) or in wheel_track (0.11 gave 0.1225 at y = 0.08, 0.12 gave 0.2725). The y = 0.08 lead was the only geometry lever that moved the oval strongly, and its gain is tied to the 0.6 kg, 0.12 m configuration. The main lesson for future work is that near-optimal designs in this simulator can be sharply sensitive to single parameters, so changes should be tested with the reproduced baseline in hand.
rationale: Iteration 10 tested wheel_track 0.11 at y = 0.08 and mass 0.6, and it failed. Oval progress fell from 0.2725 to 0.1225, the score fell from 75.92 to 54.95, and slalom still lost the line once per run (progress 0.105). The oval result is non-monotonic in both mass and track width, and the iteration 7 design is the only tested point that gives the oval gain. Iterations 7 and 9 reproduced exactly (75.9247), so the simulator is deterministic for this design. Iteration 9's telemetry also shows s-bend oscillation at 0.135 and slalom at 1.0 line loss per run, both within the limits. Because this is the final iteration and the unseen-track race is scored once, the rational choice is to deliver the proven best design rather than explore further. I restore wheel_track 0.12 and keep every other field from iteration 7: mass 0.6, forward lead y = 0.08, 16 mm sensors at x = -0.08 to 0.08 in 0.04 m steps, wheel radius 0.03, body 0.16 by 0.14 m. The Integrator's controller is unchanged. The risk is that an unseen track of a different shape behaves differently. This design is sensitive to mass and track width, so I do not recommend further tuning of geometry at this point.
